title: Bridgewater's Ray Dalio sees a trigger that could burst the AI bubble: Billionaires selling their wealth
source_used: Yahoo Finance (Brian Sozzi), citing Bloomberg's first report
key_facts: Billionaire Ray Dalio, founder of Bridgewater Associates, spoke at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026; Bloomberg first reported his comments.
Dalio suggested measures that force the ultra-wealthy to sell unrealised gains, such as a wealth tax, could hasten or contribute to a bubble bursting.
He said AI speculation may be nearing its peak: 'We're in the part of the cycle that is before that but approaching that... I think we're close to that.'
Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft together make up over 21% of the S&P 500, the most concentrated the index has been in three stocks, per Creative Planning data.
In the mid-1980s the biggest three (IBM, AT&T and ExxonMobil) made up 13.4% at their peak.
quote_evidence: Dalio suggested that measures that force the ultrawealthy to liquidate their unrealized gains, such as a wealth tax, could hasten or contribute to a bubble popping.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) has never been more concentrated in just three stocks than it is today
why_it_matters_hint: Dalio's new point is that forced selling by the very rich could be what ends an AI bubble.
notes: Follow-up of the 7 Oct 2026 item (1007:X03, Bloomberg: Dalio says the AI boom looks like a classic bubble close to bursting). New today: the wealth-tax trigger he named and Yahoo Finance's S&P 500 concentration data. Dalio's view is an opinion.
